Passing tests: 10 (all tests in the list are now implemented and green)

Recent Green phase: the scoring model was corrected. Previously the threshold constant was 4 with a per-army `countSphinxes * (...)` multiply, which was a curve-fit that only matched single-Sphinx armies. The final test (two Sphinxes, four types -> 6) exposed it. The rule is now: each Sphinx scores independently as `1 + varietyPoints(distinct types among all the OTHER cards, excluding that Sphinx's own card)`, where varietyPoints(n) = n > 3 ? 2*(n-3) : 1. The threshold is now 3, matching the card text "1 point. 2 per type beyond three, else 1". `countSphinxes` became `isSphinx`, a `withoutIndex` helper was added, and `scoreArmy` is now a reduce over the army.

Working directory: /home/experimenter/experiments/runs/2026-08-11_14-47-44_sphinx-score-example-mapping_v6.8-no-end-refactor-cc_opus-5-no-thinking

Refactor the implementation while keeping all tests green. Run tests with `pnpm test`.

Note: `withoutIndex` rebuilds an array per Sphinx, and every Sphinx in a given army actually sees the same type set. There may be a clearer formulation. Use your judgement — clarity first.

All 10 green.

**Naming Evaluation (first priority)**

- `scoreArmy` — accurate, reads well. Keep.
- `isSphinx`, `typeOf`, `varietyPoints`, `countDistinctTypes` — all reveal intent. Keep.
- `withoutIndex` — the name is honest but it names a *mechanism* (array surgery by position), not the domain concept. The domain concept it serves is "the types a Sphinx can see". That's the smell the prompt flagged.

**The insight**

Every Sphinx in an army sees the same type set. A Sphinx's own card contributes the type `sphinx`; removing one Sphinx card only removes `sphinx` from the type set when it is the *last* Sphinx in the army — and any army with two or more Sphinxes always still has a Sphinx left over. So:

- 1 Sphinx: it sees `distinctTypes(army) - 1` (its own type drops out).
- 2+ Sphinxes: each sees `distinctTypes(army)` — the other Sphinx keeps the type alive.

Per-index rebuilding is doing real work only to rediscover a fact that holds uniformly for the whole army. Computing the visible-type count once, from the army, is both clearer and removes the per-Sphinx array allocation.

**APP mass — before**

`isSphinx` 4, `typeOf` 2, `countDistinctTypes` 8, `varietyPoints` 13, `withoutIndex` 12, `scoreArmy` 24. Total **63**.

content.text:
10/10 green, typecheck clean.

## Refactoring report

**Rule 1 (Tests pass)** — 10/10 green before, after each step, and at the end. Typecheck clean.

**Rule 2 (Reveals intent)** — the main win. `withoutIndex` named a mechanism (filter an array by position) rather than a domain idea. Replaced with `typesVisibleToEachSphinx`, which states the rule the mechanism was implementing. Added `ownTypeSurvives` to name the condition, and `sphinxScore` so `scoreArmy` reads as "one Sphinx's score, once per Sphinx". `scoreArmy`, `isSphinx`, `typeOf`, `varietyPoints`, `countDistinctTypes` were already accurate — kept.

**Rule 3 (No duplication)** — the per-index rebuild was *computational* duplication: it recomputed, for each Sphinx, a type set that is provably the same for all of them. Now computed once. `countSphinxes` also de-duplicates the two `filter(isSphinx).length` sites.

**Rule 4 (Fewest elements)** — dropped `withoutIndex` and the per-Sphinx array allocation.

**The insight that made it possible.** A Sphinx drops only its own card, so the type `sphinx` still counts whenever another Sphinx remains. One Sphinx sees `distinctTypes - 1`; two or more each see `distinctTypes`. The per-index reduce was doing O(n²) work to rediscover an army-wide fact.

**Verifying it's a refactoring, not a behaviour change.** The multiply-by-count shape resembles the curve-fit the last Red phase killed, so I did not rely on the 10 tests alone. I checked the new version against the pre-refactor per-index implementation across all 55,986 armies up to length 6 over a 6-monster pool (including 2- and 3-Sphinx armies the suite never exercises): **zero mismatches**. The distinction from the old bug: that version multiplied a *wrong* per-army variety figure; this one multiplies a per-Sphinx score that is identical across Sphinxes by the argument above. The scratch script was deleted.

**APP mass: 63 → 62 (Δ −1).** Essentially flat, and that is the honest result — I extracted two new named functions (each adding bindings and an invocation at the call site, per the tool's own arithmetic) while removing `withoutIndex` and the index-threading reduce. I did not chase the number; the real gain is that the O(n²) allocation is gone and the "why" now lives in a named function instead of a comment above an array filter.

Implementation: `/home/experimenter/experiments/runs/2026-08-11_14-47-44_sphinx-score-example-mapping_v6.8-no-end-refactor-cc_opus-5-no-thinking/src/sphinx-score.ts`

One judgement call worth flagging for the next cycle: `typesVisibleToEachSphinx` encodes a derivation ("all Sphinxes see the same set") that is correct but not obvious from the card text. I verified it exhaustively and documented the reasoning in the comment, but if a future rule makes Sphinxes see different type sets — say a card that hides a type from one player — this collapses back to a per-Sphinx computation. The tests do not currently pin that assumption, since none of them can distinguish the two formulations.
